notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, in 4 of 26 matched pairs (sample syllabus statements and the data-handling rule: general vs course-start or during-work), resolved by whether the passage is a standing rule, a communication of expectations, or governs work in progress; (2) unit_stance, which is not in the agreement shares but differed on about 8 pairs (A neutral vs B permit/encourage on verification, rationale and tool-description sentences), resolved to neutral where the sentence states a procedure, fact or verification duty and takes no position on whether AI is allowed; (3) policy_type in 2 pairs: 'Some assignments prohibit AI use entirely' (P01 vs P04, resolved to P04 because it is set per assignment, not by default) and the technology-governance 'must follow' sentence (P50 vs P65, resolved to P50); (4) modality and actor in 2 pairs ('needs to be ... properly cited' resolved to must; the instructor-addressed 'please review ... training' line resolved to instructor/should). Policy wording: B left policy null far more often than A; where the anchor is a partial span of a longer sentence A's faithful normalized wording was kept. A-only units (6 kept): 'free to write your own policy', 'See individual assignment instructions', the library citation pointer, 'Effective AI use includes maintaining academic integrity' (UNCOVERED), 'important to use them responsibly and ethically', and the attribution half of an encourage sentence. One A-only unit was dropped (Copilot 'applies existing safeguards such as encryption', a descriptive restatement of the preceding kept unit). B-only unit kept: 'validate AI-generated content' (modality changed from should to informs). Stance matched on both documents (delegates; encourage). new_types empty on both sides.
